_doc: The AUTHORED config kernel — product decisions, never facts, never cited (gate 3, founder 2026-08-07→09). scriptConverter keys drive lib/scripts.js conversion; conlangs are whole product-defined locales; formality/registers entries here are the hand-enriched ones the runtime merges when a card carries none.

x-elvish-s.name: Sindarin (Tolkien Elvish)

formality.description: Sindarin is J.R.R. Tolkien's Elvish language. It has a formal/informal distinction through verb mutation and pronoun choice, but the corpus is small enough that only a general register is practical for translation. Sindarin uses Latin script for working translation; Tengwar script is available via converter.

tools.name: llm translation API
tools.description: Supported by llm for machine translation (verified date unknown).

x-elvish-s.notes: Tengwar script requires a CSUR-compatible font (PUA U+E000–E07F). Mode of Beleriand is used for the deterministic converter.

formality.description: Constructed language or stylistic variant — no formality system. Tone is defined entirely by the register preset.

standard.label: Standard Pirate
standard.description: Classic pirate English with nautical metaphors and Arr vocabulary.
standard.prompt: Pirate English. Translate into stereotypical pirate dialect with nautical vocabulary, 'ye' for 'you', 'me' for 'my', 'Arr' interjections, and seafaring metaphors. Keep UI meaning clear — the joke should enhance, not obscure, the interface. Error messages should still be understandable.

full-send.label: Full Send Pirate
full-send.description: Maximum pirate. Every sentence gets the full treatment. For themed apps and Talk Like a Pirate Day.
full-send.prompt: Maximum pirate English. Every response gets the full treatment — nautical slang, sea shanty rhythm, treasure metaphors, weather references. 'Loading' becomes 'Haulin' anchor', 'Error' becomes 'Blimey!'. Fun trumps clarity.

aliasRouting._why: Product ROUTING decisions, not facts. CLDR keeps `no` as its own locale (likelySubtags no→no-Latn-NO) and its nob→nb alias is reason 'overlong', not 'macrolanguage' — so no fetched source says no=Bokmål. Routing `no` to nob is a pre-existing product decision (Bokmål is what `no` content overwhelmingly is, and it is the tag vendors publish), relocated here from the old corpus's alias table. The 94 macrolanguage variety pins remain a founder decision; this file records only what the product already did.

evalConfig._why: OUR evaluation wiring — which LYSS package, plugin classes and eval packs the harness loads per language. Product configuration under gate 3: declared, never cited as a fact about the language.

evalStandard.description: Champollion-LYSS measurement plugins — Cree LYSS linter + semantic validator. Fetched on demand from PyPI; the harness core ships no language-specific scorer code.
evalStandard.ipNotice:
Plains Cree (nêhiyawêwin) data sovereignty — please read.

The Cree LYSS validation standard and any Plains Cree language data are treated as the property of the nêhiyaw language community and are offered for NON-COMMERCIAL, community-benefit use (sovereignty-aspirant — community ownership and control of language data; relational-trust governance in progress).

Gloss data is fetched live from the public itwêwina API (itwewina.altlab.app) and cached locally for your own use only. The underlying dictionary content (Wolvengrey CW, Maskwacîs MD, AECD) is NOT openly licensed — do not commit, redistribute, publish, or bundle the cache. The Cree FST (GiellaLT/ALTLab, AGPL) is downloaded and invoked as a separate tool, never bundled.

By installing and running this standard you agree to respect these terms. Set CHAMPOLLION_LYSS_ACCEPT_IP=1 to acknowledge in automation.
